title: Bring us back
hookLine: the next asks for return to the Torah and to God
carry: the way back was already built in

lines: THE WAY BACK FROM WHERE YOU ARE.
cards: A phone's map app has one phrase it says more patiently than any person ever could. Rerouting. You missed the exit, you took the wrong lane, you ignored it three times in a row.
It never says you idiot. It never says go home. It quietly works out the way back from exactly where you are.
The second request of the Amidah is built on the same idea. Once you understand where you are, the next thing to ask for is the way back.

teach.b: The fifth blessing says: bring us back, our Father, to Your Torah. Draw us near, our King, to Your service. Return us in complete teshuvah before You.
Blessed are You, who desires teshuvah. Teshuvah is usually translated repentance, but it shares its verb with turning, returning. It's less about feeling terrible and more about changing direction.
The blessing echoes the end of the book of Lamentations, with that same verb.

teach.h: TURN US, AND WE SHALL BE TURNED.
teach.b: In the old Jewish translation: "Turn Thou us unto Thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned." Notice the grammar: the person praying asks God to do the turning. It admits that coming back is hard to do alone.
First our Father, then our King: the close relationship comes first, then the formal one. Why does this come right after understanding?

The Talmud, in Megillah 17b, points to a verse in Isaiah that runs understanding with their heart, return, and be healed. You can't turn around until you see where you are. And the ending is gentle: God desires teshuvah.
Wants it. Elsewhere the Talmud, in Pesachim 54a, lists teshuvah among seven things created before the world itself.
Before anyone could go wrong, the way back was already built in.

how: Hashiveinu, the request for return, is the fifth blessing of the weekday Amidah; the verse from Lamentations it echoes is also sung as the Torah scroll is returned to the ark.

games.q: you're arranging the requests of the Amidah. understanding is first. what should come next?
games.why: Megillah 17b: understand with the heart, return, and be healed. once you see where you are, you can turn.

practice: Pick one place where you've drifted from who you meant to be: a habit that slipped, a friendship you let go quiet, a promise to yourself you stopped keeping.
Don't plan the whole road; just picture the first step back, one text, one page, one walk, one honest sentence, taken from exactly where you are. If you pray, you can ask for help turning.

wordCard.voice: Teshuvah. Return, turning around — what the Amidah's fifth blessing asks God to bring us back to, a way back God desires and already built in.

orig.note: Hebrew: bring us back. from sh-u-v, turn, the root of teshuvah.

carryVoice: Your line: the way back was already built in. Turning starts from right where you stand. See you tomorrow.
